  • Method Details

    • isProvideDimensionHints

      boolean isProvideDimensionHints()
      Set to true if the "dimension hints" should be provided on the "export data slice" call. This will add dimension definitions to the 'left' axis. Although the REST API documentation states that defining dimensions improves performance, it doesn't seem to make a big difference. The main reason for this being an option now is that without dimension hints, retrieves with an attribute dimension in the left/rows orientation will return invalid results (e.g., the attribute dimension axis will be lost).
      Returns:
      true if dimension hints should be provided, false otherwise

    • isExportPlanningData

      boolean isExportPlanningData()
      Whether to return supporting details with the export request.
      Returns:
      true if supporting details should be exported along with data, false otherwise

    • isSuppressMissingRows

      boolean isSuppressMissingRows()
      Whether to ask the export call to suppress missing data rows. This can significantly reduce the size of the response data, although it has a different shape than the incoming request, making it harder to merge the results with the request.
      Returns:
      true if suppress missing is enabled, false otherwise

    • isSuppressMissingColumns

      boolean isSuppressMissingColumns()
      Whether to ask the export call to suppress missing columns (this is a flag on the REST API, if not a "real" flag in traditional Essbase/Smart View/ad hoc operations).

      Note: even when this is off, it appears that if you don't have access to a member in the column orientation, then that column will be suppressed regardless. Either way, you should be prepared for a result grid to have a different shape than the request.

      Returns:
      true if column suppression is enabled, false otherwise

    • getMaxCellsPerRetrieve

      int getMaxCellsPerRetrieve()
      The max number of cells that can be brought back into a single retrieve. As of this writing, EPM cloud imposes a 500,000 cell limit on individual retrieves. This library allows to work around this by breaking larger retrieves into smaller ones, then stitching them back together.
      Returns:
      the max numbers of cells that will be allowed per retrieve before breaking them up
